props.title: Stay Wealthy
lines: Getting money and keeping money are different skills.
Survival is the strategy: stay in the game so compounding can finish.

left.name: Getting wealthy
lines: Needs taking risk, optimism, concentration, hustle.
Fails as fragility: a great return that ends in year twelve.

right.name: Staying wealthy
lines: Needs humility, useful fear, cash, frugality, room for error.
Wins as longevity: a good return that lasts fifty years beats a spectacular one that blows up.
Margin of safety is not about being right. It is about not being forced out.

props.title: Leverage turned a crash into a forced sale

rows.v: Charlie Munger and Rick Guerin were both early Buffett partners.
Guerin used leverage. In the early 1970s the market crushed him.
Berkshire fell almost 70% in those two years.
Margin calls: Guerin sold Berkshire under $40 a share. Buffett later bought some of that stock.
Buffett did not need the money, so he was not a forced seller.
Staying wealthy means arranging life so you never have to sell at the bottom.

props.kicker: CASH LOOKS DUMB UNTIL YOU NEED IT
props.title: The 1% versus 10% nag

rows.v: Illustration: cash earns 1%, stocks 10%. The 9-point gap nags every day.
The book's point: cash's real yield is not 1%. It is the option not to become a forced seller.
The book cites a housing boom and bust that touched nearly 10 million households.
A rate you can survive: '8% would be great; 4% I can still live with.'

props.title: Staying wealthy on one card
items: Frugality, cash, and low leverage are how you avoid becoming Rick Guerin in a two-year crash.
A 70% drop is a fee if you can wait. It is ruin if a lender can call the loan.
Plan for 4% years even if you hope for 8%. Room between those numbers is the strategy.
Getting rich and staying rich need different personalities. Do not let offense run the whole life.

rows.v: Getting rich can require optimism, concentration, and a willingness to look foolish for a while.
Staying rich requires paranoia about ruin: cash, frugality, and no lender who can call you at the bottom.
Rick Guerin was in the same early Buffett circle. Leverage turned a crash into an exit.
The book: do not let the personality that got you rich run the whole rest of the life.
Survive first. Compounding is only available to people who are still in the game.
